attempts.raw_response: He said the Trislander aircraft were essential for connecting the smaller islands when larger planes couldn't operate due to weather or runway constraints. The ATR72 fleet serving the main routes would remain under Blue Islands' control. Bowyer emphasised that the split would create a more focused operation better equipped to handle the unique challenges of island aviation. He added that he had the experience and knowledge to run a dedicated Trislander service safely and reliably. The proposals were expected to be considered by regulators as both companies worked to secure the future of air links between the Channel Islands and the UK mainland.
